summary:
I worked in `P/i-guard/sdkgen`, which started as a copy of `P/base/sdkgen` at `v31-frozen` (9089ed48). I added 29 commits there, all test-side. Nothing under `ts/src` or `ts/project` changed, and `ts/dist` is unchanged: `git status` is empty after a full `npm run build`.

**What I ran:**
- Guard plus reader: 61/61 (39 + 22).
- Suite without the toolchain lanes: 2593 tests, 2588 pass, 0 fail, 5 skipped.
- The last stage's 75 mutations, re-run on a copy: 65 → 67 caught, and none is caught less.
- 19 new mutations: 18 caught. The one miss is a planted gap: an excused token 8 lines from the quote (see `mutations`).

**Part 1, the reader.** The reader and the table now show, for every declaration of all twenty runtimes:
- how a failure shows (`fails`): swift `throws`, go's second `error`, c's `PNError**`, rust `Result`, zig `*Result`, lua's second value;
- what a member is called on (instance, type or module);
- whether it is a field or something called;
- whether its return was read from a comment (lua, rb);
- which parameters may be left out;
- which member families a runtime lacks.

Each language also gets a constructor and test-constructor row, and a stream line saying when the operation runs and when the streaming feature's items are read.

Three kinds of check enforce these:
- **Text invariants.** A declaration whose own text shows `throws`, `static`, `def self.` or `@classmethod` must be read that way, whatever the forms say.
- **Per-forms pins.** `failure` and `expect` hold what was read off the runtime, so a changed runtime fails the reader test even in an unported language.
- **Guard checks for providers:**
  - `fails`: the signature carries the marker, and the printed call carries the call word (go `err`, c `&err`, rust `unwrap`, zig `.err`; swift `try` is declared but untested, since swift has no provider).
  - `on`: a member declared on the type cannot be listed among instance members, and constructor and test-constructor calls must be made on what the runtime declares.
  - `field`: a field is not declared as called, and the reverse.
  - `streamItems`: a stream kind whose sentence says items arrive as iterated must match what the code does.

Reading the table against the runtimes found:
- **Stream kinds wrong in two ported languages:** clojure and elixir say `streamLazy`, but both read every item before returning. Recorded as `WRONG:`.
- **swift streams claim too much:** swift is `streamIterator` but collects every item before it returns. No stream kind fits it, so it is listed as needed from the shared engineer.
- **c's page omits two members** the runtime has: `sdk_options_map` and `sdk_get_utility`. Recorded as `WRONG:`.
- Four rows of the unported table were misread: scala `toString` (a method shown as a field), cpp's client constructor (return shown as `explicit`), kotlin's client constructor (return shown as its superclass), and ocaml's stream kind.

**Part 2, the categories.**
- `none` and `lits.*` are now cited, with the value's token required in the quote. For the 8 providers that do not declare `lits` yet, it is cited ahead of the declaration, so the merged guard fails if the shared engineer declares any other literal.
- What remains in `language` is `maps` (9 languages) and `unusedError` (go, zig).
- A citation can now be an absence: a search over named runtime files that must find nothing, run every time. All 8 `cancel: false` facts use it.
- A note's citation must hold every code token the note names.
- An `unquoted` token is refused when it stands within 3 lines of a quote. This is not the repo-wide check the brief asked for (see `gaps`).
- I audited all 113 cited facts, plus 16 cited ahead of a declaration:
  - **Changed:** 28 citations, including the 8 `cancel` absences and new `none` citations.
  - **Still not showing the value:** 3 (py and rb `direct.returns`, ts `prepare.returns`).
  - **Pinned prose:** 53.
  - **WRONG exceptions:** elixir's `list/2` and `load/2` notes; clojure's and elixir's stream kinds; c's missing options and utility members.

**Against H1:** a language now also has to supply a test-constructor name, a stream record (7 lines), and `on`, `fails` or `failure` where the defaults do not fit, plus none, lits and absence citations. Forms files grew by 10 to 22 lines each. The framework had 3 breaking changes, each forcing edits in existing forms files; everything else was additive (see `forms_changes`).

dimensions.dimension: how a failure shows (throws / second value / error parameter / Result / error union)
dimensions.how_read: Decl.fails, filled from forms.fails(d). swift reads `throws` after the bracketed parameter list; go a returns ending `error)`; c a last parameter `PNError**`; rust a returns starting `Result<`; zig a returns ending `Result`; lua a second `---@return` value. Every other runtime returns ''. The forms' `failure: {shows, call}` says what every operation shows and what a call needs.
dimensions.how_compared: Reader: every op decl's fails must include failure.shows. Operations that show a failure without a failure record fail. Any declaration whose own text has `throws` after its parameters must read as throws, whatever forms.fails says. Guard: sig() requires failure.shows in the provider's signature when the runtime declaration shows it (exception key fails:<where>). The provider's printed load call, run through S.call outside an attempt, must contain failure.call.
dimensions.negative_control: Controls 'a failure marker dropped from the load signature' and 'the printed call drops what a failing call needs' (applicable for go, c, rust, zig). Mutations new-swift-throws-runtime, new-swift-throws-view and new-swift-try-dropped: caught (reader).

dimensions.dimension: what a member is called on (instance, type, module)
dimensions.how_read: Decl.on, from forms.on(d) or the default: a constructor's name or a `static` head is on the type. Overrides: go `func (` instance else module; py __init__ or @classmethod/@staticmethod type; rb `def self.` type; lua `.name(` type and `:name(` instance; kotlin companion-object funs type; scala members of `object X` type; rust/zig `self` receiver instance, indented type, column-0 module; c `(*fn)` instance else module; perl `my ($class` type and `my ($self` instance; clojure keyword fns instance else module; elixir module; ocaml record fields instance and `let` module.
dimensions.how_compared: Reader: a `static` head, `def self.` or a @classmethod/@staticmethod line above must read as type. forms.expect pins named declarations (test constructors of js, php, lua, csharp, java, kotlin, scala, swift, cpp, perl, ocaml). Guard: a member whose runtime declaration is on the type, listed in ref.facts.client or entity, fails 'on'. The test-constructor call's receiver (the bound client variable means instance, a qualifier means type or module, nothing means free) must fit the runtime's `on`. The client constructor's call must not be on an instance.
dimensions.negative_control: Controls 'a test constructor called on an instance' (all 9) and 'a member the runtime declares on the type listed among the instance members' (ts, py, rb). Mutations new-ts-static-test-instance and new-py-classmethod-test-instance (guard 'on'), and new-swift-static-testsdk-instance (reader expect): caught.

dimensions.how_read: Decl.field: forms.field(d), default the declaration has no parameter list. ocaml's declReader marks a record field whose type has no arrow. scala treats only val/var as fields; rb never has fields and is parenless.
dimensions.how_compared: Reader: a field may not take parameters, and forms.expect pins fields (ocaml e_name, e_deleted, e_data; e_load not a field; kotlin name). Guard sig(): a runtime field declared with a call, or a runtime callable declared without a parameter list (unless forms.parenless), fails 'field'.
dimensions.negative_control: Control 'a called member declared as a field' (ts, go, py, zig, rust; n/a for c, clojure, elixir, rb). Mutation new-ocaml-field-to-function: caught (reader expect).

dimensions.dimension: a return read from a comment
dimensions.how_read: Decl.from from forms.returnsFrom: lua and rb say 'comment'. The table cell carries '(from a comment)'.
dimensions.how_compared: Shown in the table. For lua, a `shows` citation of make_error.lua states what the second value really is. For rb, the facts resting on @return are cited (uncompared returns 7).
dimensions.negative_control: None mechanical for the label itself. The lua shows citation fails if its quotes leave make_error.lua (checkCitation).

dimensions.dimension: when a stream's items are read
dimensions.how_read: forms.stream: file, construct, starts ('at call' or 'on iteration'), run, draw, and runs/items as declared. Each quote must occur exactly once in a runtime file. A run or draw quote before the construct happens before the stream returns; after it, 'as the caller iterates' (or 'from the call, beside the caller' when the construct starts at the call, go's goroutine).
dimensions.how_compared: Reader: the declared runs and items must equal what the positions give. The kind the forms read must not claim incremental items (streamIterator, streamGenerator, streamLazy) when the code reads them before returning, nor one list (streamList) when it does not; exception key streamItems. Guard: the same, against the provider's declared kind.
dimensions.negative_control: Control 'a stream recorded as read as the caller iterates when the code reads it first' (7 of 9; clojure and elixir carry WRONG exceptions). Mutations new-swift-stream-incremental, new-clojure-stream-incremental and new-ocaml-stream-incremental-code: caught (reader).

dimensions.dimension: which parameters may be left out; which member families a runtime lacks
dimensions.how_read: forms.optional on each parameter, marked '[optional]' in the table. FAMILIES not in forms.members are listed.
dimensions.how_compared: Optional was already compared by the guard ('optional'). Absent families feed the existing members check; a WRONG exception per family now exists (members:<fam>).
dimensions.negative_control: Existing control 'an optional parameter shown required'. c options and utility: a members finding unless excepted (ran).
